Entry, exit and churn rates by market

Source: R/dynamics.R
get_dynamics.Rd

Follows each organization across years and counts, for every market and year t, the organizations that entered (present in t, not in t - 1) and exited (present in t - 1, then absent for at least absent_years years). Rates use the stock in t - 1 as the denominator, with the market and subsector the organization had in t - 1 for exits and in t for entries. Organizations that move between markets count as neither.

Usage

get_dynamics(
  df,
  geography = "CBSA_FIPS",
  subsector = "NTEEV2",
  year = "YEAR",
  id = "EIN2",
  filer_type = NULL,
  revocation = "REVOCATION_YEAR",
  absent_years = 2,
  observed_years = NULL,
  drop_ppa_revocations = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame with one row per organization-year.

geography

Name of the column that identifies the market's geography, such as "CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS" or "COUNTY_FIPS".

subsector

Name of the column that identifies the subsector. When it is "NTEEV2", the first three characters (the major group) are used.

year

Name of the column that identifies the year, such as "TAXYEAR".

id

Name of the organization id column.

filer_type

Optional filer type column ("990", "990EZ", "990N", "NONFILER", ...). When given, graduation and downgrade rates are added (see Value).

revocation

Name of the revocation year column, if any; used for EXITS_PPA.

absent_years

Years of absence that confirm an exit. Use 2 or more for filers, whose filings can lapse a year; 1 for the registered universe, where absence is observed directly.

observed_years

The years df covers, which must be consecutive. Defaults to the years present in df. Pass it when some observed years are not reported, so that their absences still count.

drop_ppa_revocations

Leave revocation exits of 2010-2012 out of EXITS and the rates.

Value

A tibble with GEO, SUB, YEAR and:

N_PREV, N_CUR

Organizations in t - 1 and in t

ENTRIES, EXITS, EXITS_PPA

Counts; EXITS_PPA are exits in 2010-2012 that coincide with a revocation

ENTRY_RATE, EXIT_RATE

ENTRIES / N_PREV, EXITS / N_PREV

NET_GROWTH

(N_CUR - N_PREV) / N_PREV, which also reflects moves between markets

CHURN_RATE

(ENTRIES + EXITS) / N_PREV

N_PREV_GRASSROOTS, GRADUATIONS, GRADUATION_RATE

With filer_type: 990-N filers and non-filers in t - 1, how many filed a 990 or 990-EZ in t, and the share

N_PREV_FILERS, DOWNGRADES, DOWNGRADE_RATE

With filer_type: 990 and 990-EZ filers in t - 1, how many were 990-N filers or non-filers in t, and the share

Rates are NA where N_PREV is 0.

What an exit means

In the filers universe an exit is an exit from filing: an organization that stops filing a Form 990 or 990-EZ may have dropped below the filing threshold and switched to the 990-N postcard, so an exit is not a death. In the registered universe an exit is removal from the IRS registry: revocation, termination or merger.

Gaps and censoring

Absences shorter than absent_years between two appearances are filled: the organization counts as present, so a late or missed filing is neither an exit nor a re-entry. A longer absence ends with a re-entry. Exits in the last absent_years - 1 observed years cannot be confirmed yet and are reported as NA, as are all rates for the first observed year, which has no prior year.

Mass revocations of 2010-2012

The Pension Protection Act revoked the exemptions of hundreds of thousands of organizations that had not filed for three years, almost all of them in 2010-2012. EXITS_PPA counts exits in those years that coincide with a revocation. drop_ppa_revocations = TRUE leaves them out of EXITS and the rates.

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  EIN2 = c( "a", "a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c", "d", "d" ),
  GEO  = "X", SUB = "ART",
  YEAR = c( 2018:2021, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2018, 2020 ) )
# a: present throughout; b: exits after 2019; c: enters in 2020;
# d: misses 2019 (filled as present with absent_years = 2), then gone
# after 2020, which cannot be confirmed as an exit until 2022
get_dynamics( d, geography = "GEO", subsector = "SUB", year = "YEAR",
              absent_years = 2 )
#> # A tibble: 12 × 12

#>  2 ALL   ALL    2020      3     3       1     1         0      0.333     0.333
#>  3 ALL   ALL    2021      3     2       0    NA        NA      0        NA    
#>  4 ALL   ART    2019      3     3       0     0         0      0         0    
#>  5 ALL   ART    2020      3     3       1     1         0      0.333     0.333
#>  6 ALL   ART    2021      3     2       0    NA        NA      0        NA
